result:
If I could change one thing about the world, I think I'd want people to have an easier time actually understanding each other—not just exchanging words, but really grasping why someone else sees things differently.

So much conflict, cruelty, and suffering seems to trace back to people being unable or unwilling to imagine their way into someone else's experience. Wars, prejudice, broken relationships, political gridlock—a lot of it has this quality of people talking past each other, certain of their own rightness, unable to see how the situation looks from another vantage point.

I don't mean everyone would suddenly agree on everything—disagreement is fine, even valuable. I mean something more like: people could disagree while still really seeing each other, rather than flattening one another into caricatures.

That said, I hold this loosely. It's the kind of question where I notice I'm reaching for something that sounds good rather than necessarily being the most important lever. Someone focused on material suffering might say the obvious answer is eliminating poverty or disease. Someone else might say the deep issue is something structural, like how power and resources get distributed.

What draws you to ask? I'm curious whether you have an answer of your own, or what's prompting the question.
